_note: Reference facts for gold buying. Each entry states HOW it was verified. Computed values show their formula. No spot-price snapshots are stored (they go stale); the calculator takes a user-supplied price with an LBMA link.

karat_definition.note: Pure (fine) gold is 24 karat. Retailers state the same figures on official education pages (linked for manual review).

troy_ounce.verification: Figure read on the official LBMA 'Troy Ounce' page (fetched 2026-10-22): '1 troy ounce = 31.1034768 grams (exactly)'. Same figure published by NIST for precious-metal conversions (linked for manual review).

lbma_price_method.summary: The LBMA Gold Price is set twice daily in auctions (10:30 and 15:00 London time), independently operated and administered by ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA), in US dollars. Prices in sterling/euro are indicative, for settlement only. Benchmarks are not published on weekends or UK bank holidays. Real-time/historical benchmark data requires a licence from IBA.
lbma_price_method.verification: Read on the official LBMA Precious Metal Prices page (fetched 2026-10-22).
lbma_price_method.snapshot_note: No price snapshot is stored on this site. Enter the current price yourself in the calculator from the LBMA page or your broker quote, and record the date/time.

hallmark_law.title: National Gold and Silver Stamping Act — fineness tolerances (15 U.S.C. § 295)
hallmark_law.summary: Gold articles must not test more than 3 parts per thousand below the stamped fineness (solder-free portion); the whole article including solder must not test more than 3ppt below (watchcases, flatware) or 7ppt below (all other articles) the mark.

hallmark_law.title: Stamping Act — maker's mark required with any quality mark (15 U.S.C. § 297(b))
hallmark_law.summary: Anyone who applies (or imports an article bearing) a quality mark stating gold content must also apply their registered trademark or name — by the same means, in type at least as large, as close as possible to the quality mark.

hallmark_law.title: FTC Jewelry Guides — gold content (16 CFR § 23.3)
hallmark_law.summary: Misrepresenting gold presence, quantity, or karat fineness is unfair/deceptive. A karat designation must immediately precede the word 'Gold' with at least equal conspicuousness (e.g., '14 Karat Gold'). Hollow-center gold-alloy products must disclose it and must NOT be called 'solid'. Gold plate/filled/overlay/rolled and electroplate have specific fineness, thickness, and disclosure rules.

hallmark_law.title: FTC Jewelry Guides — vermeil (16 CFR § 23.4)
hallmark_law.summary: 'Vermeil' means a sterling-silver base coated on all significant surfaces with gold (or ≥10K gold alloy) of reasonable durability and at least 2.5 microns of fine gold. A base-metal layer under the gold must be disclosed.
